analyses.failure: test_chk_020_wrong_opcode_source — CHK-010: expected o_apb_pslverr=1 at cycle 157 got 0 (sim.log:41, SVA NNC_FAIL CHK-010 @4800000 sim.log:138)
analyses.spec_says: spec/m_apb_tlul_bridge_Design_Specification.md:132 REQ-ERR-005: "When the TL-UL response has d_source different from PARA_SRC_ID, the bridge shall complete the APB transfer with PSLVERR = 1." Spec:402 defines w_resp_err = "i_tlul_d_error or (i_tlul_d_opcode differs from (reg_a_rd ? 3'b001 : 3'b000)) or (i_tlul_d_source differs from PARA_SRC_ID)". Spec:167 says the D-channel checker in m_tlul_if "checks d_error, d_opcode, d_source". Spec:178, :274, :410 (OP-004), :474 (ERR-005) and :703 (DEC-008, which the designer confirmed on 2026-10-18) say the same. rules.json:1208-1213 (BR-3-28) quotes REQ-ERR-005 as MUST. contract.json:535 (CHK-010) has err including (i_tlul_d_source != PARA_SRC_ID), and contract.json:749-750 (CHK-020) expects PSLVERR=1, PRDATA=0 for a wrong-source response.
analyses.rtl_does: rtl/m_tlul_if.sv:99-100: `w_exp_opcode = reg_a_rd ? 1 : 0; w_resp_err = i_tlul_d_error | (i_tlul_d_opcode != w_exp_opcode);`. The d_source compare is missing. i_tlul_d_source is declared as an input at m_tlul_if.sv:46 and connected at m_apb_tlul_bridge.sv:125, but nothing in m_tlul_if uses it. The comment at m_tlul_if.sv:97-98 says "d_source must echo the constant source identifier", but the code does not do that. When a response has the correct opcode, d_error=0 and d_source=PARA_SRC_ID^1, w_resp_err=0. m_apb_if.sv:115-118 then loads reg_pslverr<=0 and reg_prdata<=i_resp_rdata. That gives o_apb_pslverr=0 at E+1 (and d_data on PRDATA for a read), where 1 and 0 are expected.
analyses.test_does: verif/tests/test_apb_tlul_bridge.py:783-788 builds 7 wrong-opcode reads and 7 wrong-opcode writes, then 4 transfers with resp="src" (w=0,1,0,1), correct opcode and d_error=0. The device drives i_tlul_d_source = t.bad_src = (SRC_ID ^ 1) & SRC_MASK (lines 113, 399-401). A correct read follows each one (lines 790-793). The monitor (lines 273-279) computes err = d_error or d_opcode != exp_op or d_source != SRC_ID, so for the src cases it expects pslverr=1 at E+1 and checks this at lines 224-228. This matches the CHK-010 contract text. The fail time is 4805 ns from a 3220 ns start, about 158 cycles, close to the end of the 1585 ns test. So the 14 wrong-opcode pairs passed and the first wrong-source transfer failed. That is an inference from timing only; the log has no per-cycle trace. The SVA a_CHK_010 (verif/sva/nnc_chk_cross.sv:72-73, 129-134) uses the same err definition and also fired at 4800000 ps.

candidates.evidence_for: The spec, the requirement, the internal-signal definition (spec:402) and the designer decision DEC-008 (spec:703) all require d_source in the error check. The RTL error expression (m_tlul_if.sv:100) leaves it out, and i_tlul_d_source has no reader at all. The RTL's own comment (m_tlul_if.sv:97-98) says the source must be checked. The wrong-opcode and d_error checks work: test_chk_019 passes (sim.log:119) and the wrong-opcode part of chk_020 runs without failing. That isolates the source compare as the only missing term.
candidates.evidence_against: None in the files. No spec text says d_source can be ignored.

analyses.test_does: verif/tests/test_apb_tlul_bridge.py:1130-1157 runs 10000 transfers from gen_random (line 690). Some of them have resp="src" (line 711), and the device then drives i_tlul_d_source=bad_src=SRC_ID^1 (lines 113, 399-401). The monitor derives err the same way as before (lines 273-279) and asserts pslverr=1 at E+1 (lines 224-228). The run stops at the first failure, cycle 311 (66430 ns, about 3125 ns into the test; sim.log:84, :129). The SVA a_CHK_010 also fails at 66425000 ps. It is the only other CHK-010 SVA failure (fails=2 in total, sim.log:191), so both SVA failures line up one-to-one with the two test failures.

candidates.evidence_for: Same root cause as test_chk_020: the RTL has no d_source term in w_resp_err (m_tlul_if.sv:100), and i_tlul_d_source is unused. The CHK-010 SVA has 3554 hits and fails only twice, both at the same times as the test failures. That fits a missing error term that only matters for the rare 'src' responses, not a general mapping bug.
candidates.evidence_against: The log does not print the transfer descriptor for cycle 311, so it is not proven that this transfer is resp="src". The other error kinds (derr, op) are covered by RTL logic that passes chk_019 and the opcode half of chk_020, which makes 'src' by far the most likely trigger.

candidates.evidence_for: With 5% orphan injection (lines 1139-1154), a monitor bookkeeping error could in theory cause a false expectation.
candidates.evidence_against: The pending/counted model in the monitor (lines 271-285) matches the independent SVA (nnc_chk_cross.sv:69-91), and both fail at the same time. If there is a counted response at E ... then at E+1: o_apb_pready=1, o_apb_pslverr=err, and o_apb_prdata = i_tlul_d_data(E) when exp_get=1 and err=0, else 32'h0." analyses.rtl_does: rtl/m_tlul_if.sv:99-100 computes the error from d_error and d_opcode only. i_tlul_d_source (line 46) is never read. m_apb_if.sv:115-118 registers pslverr<=i_resp_err and prdata<=i_resp_rdata (m_tlul_if.sv:105: d_data on a read with no error). So for a wrong-source response, o_apb_pslverr=0 at E+1, and on a read o_apb_prdata=d_data where 0 is expected.
